clue.text: Plot main crime with leading criminals

indicators.note: the criminals go at the front, leading the other piece

parts.note: cons is short for convicts, so criminals
the main is the open sea, and crime on the high seas is piracy

explanation.surface: Gang leaders hatch a scheme for some major criminal enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the old word for the open sea, not an adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy is a secret scheme, which is what a plot is.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot a fowl

definitions.meaning: to raise its hammer ready to fire

explanation.definitionFit: Raising a gun's hammer readies it for firing, and a rooster is a farmyard bird.

clue.text: Lacking go-ahead, retreat

parts.note: no means without, lacking
OK is approval, the go-ahead

explanation.surface: Refused permission, someone withdraws.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a secluded corner one can withdraw to, a hideaway.

clue.text: Bridges, for example, necessary to operate a lute

indicators.note: the letters must be worked over, as if something were necessary to rearrange them

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Bridges is told a musician must be able to play a lute.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Bridges held the post of national laureate from 1913 to 1930; the capital B disguises a surname as engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Bridges was an English poet appointed to the royal office of national poet, so he is an instance.

clue.text: Having bad weather, though there's a little sunshine round home

indicators.note: the sunbeam goes around the word for home, enclosing it

parts.note: a ray is a small beam of sunlight
in means at home

explanation.surface: Even in a dismal spell there is a glimmer of sun around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home' as IN is the at-home sense, as in 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet, showery days are the commonest kind of foul weather.

clue.text: Red ridge in black rock

indicators.note: the ridge is placed inside the black rock

parts.note: coal is black rock dug from mines
a chine is a ridge, as of land or a backbone

explanation.surface: A red seam shows in a dark outcrop.
explanation.walkthrough: A chine is a mountain ridge or backbone; 'Red' is the whole definition, the dye named for its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson dye made from insects, so the colour scarlet.

clue.text: In work, ring Douglas's pet?

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, whose Manx cats have no tail, so a puss lacking its last letter

explanation.surface: At work, someone phones about the cat belonging to a man called Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is not a person but the capital of the Isle of Man; a Manx cat is tailless, so PUSS loses its end to give PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is the Latin for a piece of work, used of a composer's numbered compositions.

clue.text: Tailor looking out for lady wanting dress

definitions.text: Tailor looking out for lady wanting dress

parts.words: Tailor looking out for lady wanting dress
parts.note: in the Godiva legend a Coventry tailor peered at the naked lady as she rode through town, and was struck blind

explanation.surface: A dressmaker keeps watch for a customer who needs a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting dress' reads as needing a gown but means unclothed, as Lady Godiva was.
explanation.definitionFit: The tailor who spied on Lady Godiva gave his name to any voyeur.

clue.text: Arrange piano music for live entertainment

parts.note: to stage an event is to arrange it
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
lays are songs, pieces of music

explanation.surface: Someone orchestrates piano music for a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage plays are dramas performed in front of an audience in person.

clue.text: Many really like a problem, one of the knotty sort

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a large number
to love is to really like
a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: Many people treat a difficulty as something to enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knotty' looks like it means tricky, but here it means a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a type of knot used to fasten a rope to a post.

clue.text: High point in game — same save repeated

indicators.note: the answer lies inside these words of the clue
the same run of letters appears twice, in game same and again in same save

explanation.surface: A football commentator hails the high spot of a match: a second identical save.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in gaME SAme and again in saME SAve, which is why the clue says 'repeated'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesa is a flat-topped hill rising steeply above a plain, an elevated spot.

clue.text: Traditional way to teach rhymes

definitions.meaning: the old method of a teacher writing on a blackboard and lecturing
a description of the phrase itself, whose two key words have the same sound

explanation.definitionFit: Blackboard and lecture is the old-fashioned teaching style, and its words chime together.

clue.text: Live dangerously, and enjoy games and matches?

definitions.meaning: taken literally: amuse oneself with matches and a blaze

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means courting risk; literally it is a child toying with a flame.

clue.text: Socially privileged, like an Oxford don's three sisters

definitions.text: like an Oxford don's three sisters
definitions.meaning: in Lewis Carroll's Alice, the Dormouse tells of three sisters who lived at the bottom of a deep shaft for water

explanation.definitionFit: Being in a good position socially; Carroll's three sisters were literally put down a shaft.

clue.text: Not inclined to be trustworthy

explanation.definitionFit: It means vertical, not leaning, and also honest, without deceit.

clue.text: Followers burst out in anger

indicators.note: the shuffled word goes inside the verb for anger

parts.note: to anger is to enrage

indicators.note: something burst is broken apart, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Supporters explode with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anger' looks like the fodder for 'burst', but it is the verb ENRAGE, and only 'out' is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants who accompany an important person.

clue.text: A motorist beginning in one country or another

indicators.note: the A and the learner go inside the first country

parts.note: Austria, a country in central Europe
L is the plate for a learner, a beginning motorist

explanation.surface: A new driver starts out in one land or another.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver shows an L plate, so 'motorist beginning' is L, not the first letter of motorist. AL goes inside AUSTRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a country, the 'another' that pairs with the first one.

clue.text: Constitutional product of member, a Liberal

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Liberal member of parliament produces something within the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constitutional is permitted by the law of the state, lawful.

clue.text: Pound up front — moderate rent

indicators.note: the pound goes at the front of the other piece

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound
to ease is to moderate or lessen

explanation.surface: A landlord wants a pound in advance in return for lower rent.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease is to rent property under a contract.

clue.text: Preserve a politician liable to change abruptly

parts.note: salt preserves food, so to salt is to preserve
a Tory is a Conservative politician in Britain

explanation.surface: Keeping a politician sweet is risky because they may switch sides suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltatory means proceeding by leaps rather than gradually, from the Latin for jumping.

clue.text: Half of MCC ruined by ill-judged charge?

definitions.text: Half of MCC ruined by ill-judged charge?

parts.words: Half of MCC ruined by ill-judged charge?
parts.note: MCC is 1200 in Roman numerals, half of it 600: the six hundred cavalrymen of Tennyson's poem, sent into a doomed attack at Balaclava in 1854

explanation.surface: Half a cricket club's team is wrecked by a reckless rush.
explanation.walkthrough: MCC looks like the Marylebone Cricket Club, the body governing English cricket, but it is a Roman number.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charge of the Light Brigade was a disastrous British cavalry attack in the Crimean War, of 'the six hundred'.

clue.text: You could take an iron for one of these birdies

definitions.text: You could take an iron for one of these birdies

parts.words: You could take an iron for one of these birdies
parts.note: a tailor's pressing iron with a curved handle is called a goose, so an iron could be mistaken for one of these birds; golfers also take an iron for a birdie

explanation.surface: A golfer reaches for an iron club to score a birdie.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture is the misdirection: 'birdies' just means birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor's smoothing iron is called a goose, plural the same as the farmyard birds.

clue.text: Accurately reproducing guy's rhymes

definitions.meaning: high fidelity sound equipment reproduces recordings faithfully
two short syllables that rhyme with the word guy

explanation.definitionFit: High-fidelity audio gives faithful reproduction of sound, and each half chimes with 'guy'.

clue.text: Joint support for proposer?

definitions.meaning: the hinge between thigh and shin
a man proposing marriage traditionally goes down on one

explanation.definitionFit: It is the leg's middle hinge, on which a suitor kneels to ask for a hand in marriage.

clue.text: Whip-round for the old statesman

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, the cat
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A collection is taken for a retired elder statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder was a Roman politician famed for his stern morality.

clue.text: Breaking away from rest in a race

indicators.note: the word for rest goes inside the phrase meaning a race

parts.note: a nation is a people, a race
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: A runner pulls clear of the field during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is a people, not a running contest, so the sporting picture misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is estrangement, the process of becoming separated from others.

clue.text: Not keeping off the grass? That's stupid!

definitions.meaning: grass is slang for cannabis, so this means taking dope

explanation.definitionFit: Dope is cannabis, so a user is drugged; dopy also means dim-witted.

clue.text: What reader may need first — to get cuttings?

definitions.text: What reader may need first — to get cuttings?

parts.words: What reader may need first — to get cuttings?
parts.note: before reading an uncut book or newspaper one may need a blade to slit the pages, or to take clippings

explanation.surface: A reader needs something before cutting out articles.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper knife is a blunt blade for slitting envelopes and uncut book pages.
